title: Abortion in Germany: arranging advice, care and follow-up
intro: This article concerns care in Germany. Abortion access depends on the legal route, pregnancy duration and clinical circumstances. Contact a recognised counselling service or an abortion provider early, even if you are undecided. They can clarify dates, appointments, costs and support without requiring you to know the whole process beforehand. Rules described here must not be assumed to apply in another country.

sections.heading: Clarify the legal route and the pregnancy dates
paragraphs: Under Germany's counselling route, exemption from punishment requires specified conditions, including counselling at a state-recognised pregnancy-conflict centre, the required certificate and a doctor performing the abortion within twelve weeks after conception. This is usually described as fourteen weeks from the start of the last period. Three full calendar days must lie between counselling and the abortion. Medical and criminological indications follow different requirements. Ask the service to confirm your route and dates rather than calculating the deadline alone.

sections.heading: Find counselling and a provider early
paragraphs: Check that the counselling centre issues the certificate needed for the counselling route; not every pregnancy advice service does. Ask for interpreting, accessibility and confidential contact arrangements if needed. Counselling and treatment appointments are separate, so also confirm where the procedure can be provided and what documents to bring. Discuss fees and possible cost coverage before treatment, including any application required. Do not delay seeking advice because you are unsure about insurance, money or the decision itself.

sections.heading: Compare the available methods with the clinical team
paragraphs: Medication and procedural abortion are different options, and availability depends on pregnancy duration and health factors. Medication causes the pregnancy to pass with cramping and bleeding; a procedural approach commonly uses suction through the cervix. Ask about pain relief, anaesthesia where relevant, expected bleeding, visits and support at home. Tell the team about medicines, allergies and medical conditions. An online article cannot establish that a pregnancy is located in the womb or that a particular method is suitable.

sections.heading: Make a clear plan for recovery and urgent symptoms
paragraphs: Get written instructions about medicines, activity, follow-up and a contact if symptoms worry you. Ask what bleeding and pain are expected and how completion will be checked. Heavy bleeding, fainting, severe or worsening abdominal pain, fever or feeling very unwell need urgent medical advice; collapse or other critical illness needs emergency help. Severe one-sided pain or fainting in someone who may be pregnant also needs urgent assessment before any scheduled counselling. Do not wait for routine appointments when acutely unwell.

sections.heading: Include emotional support and future preferences
paragraphs: People can experience relief, sadness, mixed feelings or little emotional change. Support should respect your choices and avoid pressure from others. Ask for a private discussion if you feel coerced or unsafe. Fertility can return soon after abortion, so discuss contraception if you want it, without making it a condition of care. If symptoms persist or the planned follow-up is unclear, contact the provider. Local services can also help with practical concerns and ongoing emotional support.

examples.title: Hypothetical example: uncertain dates
examples.text: A person is unsure when their last period began. They contact a recognised centre and a provider promptly, explain the uncertainty and arrange assessment. They do not assume that an online estimate guarantees enough time for the required steps.

examples.title: Hypothetical example: planning the return home
examples.text: Before treatment, a patient asks about travel, pain relief, help at home and the number to call after hours. They confirm the follow-up method and ask about cost assistance before the appointment rather than waiting until the procedure day.

questions: Which legal route applies, how are my pregnancy dates assessed and what appointments or certificate do I need?
Which methods suit my circumstances, and what are their risks, pain relief options and costs?
How will completion be confirmed, which symptoms need urgent care and whom can I contact?
